symptoms: Uniform creamy-white body, active movement, healthy appetite, normal molting at expected intervals.
favorable_weather: Maintain 24-26°C temperature and 75-85% humidity with good ventilation.
organic_control: No treatment needed. Continue regular monitoring, hygiene and standard feeding schedule.
cultural_practice: Maintain rearing-bed hygiene, provide fresh mulberry leaves, monitor after every feed.
prevention: Disinfect rearing trays between batches, avoid overcrowding, isolate any worm showing unusual color or behavior immediately.

symptoms: Inter-segmental swelling, body becomes glossy/yellowish, restless wandering before death, body ruptures easily releasing milky fluid.
cause: Viral infection (Bombyx mori Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus - BmNPV), spreads rapidly through contaminated rearing beds, tools, and other infected worms.
favorable_weather: High humidity, poor ventilation, overcrowded rearing beds, contaminated leaf or equipment.
organic_control: Not treatable once infected - remove and destroy infected larvae immediately (do not compost near rearing area). Disinfect the entire rearing bed and tools with 2% formalin or bleaching powder solution.
chemical_control: No chemical cure exists - this is a viral disease. Isolation and disinfection are the only effective response.
cultural_practice: Isolate infected larvae the moment symptoms appear; disinfect trays, stands and tools between every batch; avoid overcrowding; ensure good ventilation.
prevention: Use disease-free layings (DFLs) from certified sources, maintain strict rearing-house hygiene, disinfect before each new batch, avoid mixing worms from different batches.
dosage_note: Formalin/bleaching powder disinfection per standard sericulture department guidelines - confirm exact dilution with your local extension officer.
expert_escalation_condition: If more than 10% of a batch shows symptoms, or symptoms appear within the first 2 days of a new instar - contact your sericulture extension officer promptly, this spreads fast.

symptoms: Visible signs of poor health that don't clearly match Grasserie's specific pattern - could be Flacherie (soft, watery, foul-smelling body), Muscardine (body turning white/hard, fungal), Pébrine (small black pepper-like spots), or another stress/disease cause.
cause: Multiple possible causes - bacterial (Flacherie), fungal (Muscardine), protozoan (Pébrine), poor-quality feed, or environmental stress. This model flags worms that look unwell without pinpointing which specific disease is responsible.
favorable_weather: Varies by underlying cause - generally high humidity, poor hygiene, or temperature stress increase risk of most silkworm diseases.
organic_control: Isolate affected larvae immediately as a precaution. Improve bed hygiene and ventilation. Do not act on chemical treatment without confirming the specific disease.
chemical_control: Not recommended until the specific disease is confirmed - treatments differ by cause and a wrong treatment wastes time on a spreading problem.
cultural_practice: Isolate affected worms, disinfect the bed, improve ventilation and humidity control while awaiting expert confirmation.
prevention: Same as Grasserie: certified disease-free layings, strict hygiene, disinfection between batches, avoid overcrowding.
dosage_note: Not applicable until the specific disease is identified.
expert_escalation_condition: Recommended for every result in this category - the AI model detects that something is wrong but cannot yet distinguish which specific disease it is. Submit to Expert with a clear photo for a confirmed diagnosis.
